## What is Quarto?

Quarto is an open-source scientific and technical publishing system that allows you to:

- Create dynamic documents with code and narrative
- Make presentations, reports, websites, and books
- Use R, Python, or other languages
- Mix code, output, and written content seamlessly

Perfect for final projects where you want to showcase analysis and code!

## Why Use Quarto for Your Presentation?

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="50%"}
**Advantages**
- Code and results live together
- Easy to update when data changes
- Professional looking slides
- Version control friendly
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
**Great for Projects**
- Show your analysis process
- Display code and output
- Include interactive elements
- Reproducible results
:::

::::

## Getting Started

**Installation:**
```
# Install Quarto from https://quarto.org/docs/get-started/
# Quarto works with RStudio
```

**Create a new presentation:**
- File → New File → Quarto Presentation
- Choose "Reveal JS" format
- Save with `.qmd` extension

## File Structure Basics

```
presentation.qmd
├── YAML Header (---...---)
│   ├── title, author, date
│   └── format options
├── Slide 1 (## heading)
├── Slide 2 (## heading)
└── More slides...
```

**Key point:** Each `##` heading creates a new slide

## YAML Header Explained

```yaml
---
title: "My Presentation"
author: "Your Name"
format: 
  revealjs:
    theme: default
    slide-number: true
    footer: "My Footer"
---
```

This section controls:
- Metadata (title, author, date)
- Output format and appearance
- Code execution options

## Creating Slides

**Slide with heading only:**
```markdown
## Slide Title
```

**Slide with content:**
```markdown
## My Slide

Content goes here. You can write text, add bullets, code, etc.
```

**Nested headings:**
```markdown
### Subheading (creates indented slide)
```

## Text Formatting

Basic formatting in your slides:

- **Bold text:** `**bold**`
- *Italic text:* `*italic*`
- `Code text:` backticks
- [Links:](https://quarto.org) `[text](url)`
- Bullet points with `-` or `*`
- Numbered lists with `1.`, `2.`, etc.

## Adding Bullet Points

Simple bullets on a slide:

- First point
- Second point
  - Nested sub-point
  - Another sub-point
- Third point

Use hyphens or asterisks, indent for nesting

## Code Chunks in Slides

Include R or Python code:

```{r}
# Example R code
x <- c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5)
mean(x)
```

The output displays below the code

## Code Chunk Options

Control what appears in slides:

```{r}
#| echo: true      # Show the code
#| eval: true      # Run the code
#| fig-width: 8    # Figure width
#| fig-height: 6   # Figure height
```

Common options:
- `echo: false` - Hide code, show output only
- `eval: false` - Show code, don't run it
- `warning: false` - Hide warnings
- `message: false` - Hide messages

## Including Graphics - Method 1

**Using `![](path)` markdown syntax:**

```markdown
![Alt text here](images/my-plot.png)
```

Simple and clean

## Including Graphics - Method 2

**Using `knitr::include_graphics()`:**

```{r}
#| fig-alt: "Description for accessibility"
knitr::include_graphics("images/my-plot.png")
```

Good for captions and accessibility

## Including Graphics - Method 3

**Generate plots directly from code:**

```{r}
plot(1:10, 1:10)
```

Plot displays automatically below code

## Creating Tables - Method 1

**Using `knitr::kable()`:**

```{r}
df <- data.frame(Name = c("Alice", "Bob"), Score = c(95, 87))
knitr::kable(df)
```

Simple and clean formatting

## Creating Tables - Method 2

**Using `kableExtra` for styled tables:**

```{r}
library(kableExtra)
kable(df) %>% 
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = "striped")
```

More customization options available

## Creating Tables - Method 3

**Markdown tables for static content:**

```markdown
| Name  | Score |
|-------|-------|
| Alice | 95    |
| Bob   | 87    |
```

Use [markdown table generator](https://www.tablesgenerator.com/markdown_tables)

::::

## Incremental Slides (Reveal One by One)

With `incremental: true` in header, bullets appear one at a time:

- Click to see first point
- Click to see second point
- Click to see third point

Toggle per-slide with `incremental: false` in code fence

## Speaker Notes

Add notes that only you see:

```markdown
## My Slide

Visible slide content

::: notes
Speaker notes go here. 
These won't appear on the slides.
:::
```

## Emphasizing Content

Make important content stand out:

- **Bold** for emphasis
- *Italics* for terms
- `code` for technical terms
- > Blockquotes for quotes or key points

## Slide Themes

Change appearance with themes:

```yaml
format:
  revealjs:
    theme: default  # or sky, beige, black, league, etc.
```

See all themes: [Quarto themes](https://quarto.org/docs/output-formats/html-themes.html)

## Rendering Your Presentation

**In RStudio:**
- Click "Render" button (or `Ctrl/Cmd + Shift + K`)
- Opens HTML preview in viewer

**From command line:**
```bash
quarto render presentation.qmd
```

Creates `presentation.html` file to share

## Organizing Your Project

Suggested structure for final projects:

```
my-project/
├── presentation.qmd      # Your slides
├── data/
│   └── data.csv
├── images/
│   └── plots.png
└── README.md
```

Keep files organized for easy access in YAML paths

## Best Practices for Final Projects

**Content:**
- Tell a story with your data
- Start with motivation/question
- Show your analysis process
- End with conclusions

**Code:**
- Hide setup code (`echo: false`)
- Show important analysis code
- Comment your code
- Use meaningful variable names

## Best Practices Continued

**Design:**
- Limit text per slide (not a document!)
- Use visuals (plots, tables, images)
- Consistent formatting
- Large readable fonts
- Avoid cluttered slides
